note: Pinned revisions of the sibling repositories sb3-creator's cross-repo gates consume. CI checks these exact commits out beside the repo (.github/workflows/ci.yml) so the gates RUN rather than skip; test/helpers/siblings.mjs turns an absent sibling into a failure when CI=true. Update a pin deliberately, in its own commit, with the suite green against it. `rev` MUST be the FULL 40-character SHA: actions/checkout only recognises a full SHA as a commit, and turns anything shorter into `git fetch origin +refs/heads/<ref>*` — a branch glob that matches nothing. An abbreviated pin here took every CI run on main down at the checkout step, before lint, tests, the mutation prover or the build ran at all. gate-integrity asserts the length; `revShort` exists only for prose.

bw-board.why: the device/board simulator the gallery e2e and physics gates drive. Advanced from 6571648 to 338ac5d, and the bump is FORCED by this repo's own ratchet rather than routine: bench-invariants carried two open 'invented terminal' endpoints, both mcu1.P4.7 in 60-retro-console's STC12 variants, because bw-circuit-ui's generic mcu catalog names PDIP-40 pin 9 RST and the bench wires P4.7. MEASURED through the engine before choosing anything, a fresh board per drive: setPin('P4.7') moves the buzzer PNP's base net (r1.a 4.990020 idle -> 0.103865 low -> 5.000000 high, collector 0 -> 4.795205), setPin('RST') was bit-identical to a nonexistent-terminal control at 4.990020 on every mode. So the engine modelled that pin as a GPIO under one spelling only, and the 8051 adapter emits P${port}.${bit} — P4.7 is the name a write to P4^7 arrives under. 3160a10 declares pin 9's two datasheet names as ONE pin with a unique-match rule (the alias fires only when the part declares exactly one of the pair, so it can never merge terminals a netlist kept apart; the declared spelling always outranks the alias) and routes every electrical MCU-terminal lookup through one helper — the MNA path, both closed-form source traces, and the two DRC checks — with a hand oracle (5*25/1025 = 0.1219512195121951) and three mutations. 338ac5d exports that table so bench-invariants can ASK the engine which two names are one pin instead of re-declaring the pair. Corpus census at the previous pair: 2163 circuit files, exactly three kind-'mcu' parts name either spelling and ZERO name both, so the ambiguous case does not occur and nothing previously driven is driven differently. The range also carries other lanes' landed work — 1987d6d (74C922 physical keypad matrix), b6df775 (the E4.1 hazard oracle), e537bd7+9b2fc40+5f79057 (open drain on both tiers, corpus impact counted as zero: OTYPER is absent from the codegen vocabulary), and 3f47825 (the double-entry repair and the tightened band) — all validated against this corpus at this pin before the bump.

bw-circuit-ui.why: the canonical circuit model, engine, and the ONE wire-endpoint dialect reader the corpus gates read circuit.json through. Advanced from 06c7ea7 (the stm32f030-part commit) to master's tip: the attiny88 pa0->gnd2 migration on this side (be6361d + ea91228 — a saved terminals array is now resolved against what the engine offers NOW, which is what carries the 135 shipped circuits forward), D21 meter input impedance (3f1d194 — a meter is 10 MOhm and no longer empties the board), per-channel V/div and FFT (7696656), worker sweeps (134cad0), and fbe7338, which is the one to know about: engineKindFor tested `typeof eng.hasDevice === 'function'` and the engine has never exported hasDevice, so EVERY passthrough kind silently collapsed to a generic 'mcu'. With that fixed, a board kind reaches the solver as its registered device, and a board-kind device drives only the GPIO terminals the part DECLARES — which found six benches in this corpus whose uno1 declared `terminals: ["gnd2"]` while wiring D13/D9/A0/D2/D12, repaired in the same commit as this bump. Corpus measured against exactly this pair: 2635 claims, compared 1239, mismatched 1, identical to 1caf851+06c7ea7 claim for claim, on 2026-08-29. LEDGERED 2026-08-29 (fab-sbx), because this bump's entry named six commits and omitted the two seating-shaped ones, and their absence was later read as an unrecorded behaviour change in 60-retro-console and 61-console-pong. Both are accounted for and NEITHER moves this corpus. e58d528 ("A board that cannot be seated must not load as seated") drops a stored seat whose KIND has no breadboard footprint; its own commit message measures the blast radius as 61 of 9011 seated parts, ALL arduino_uno, and this corpus has none left seated because scripts/normalize-controller-seating.mjs already re-authored them. 01101a2 ("Placement that knows how big the part is") changes only the designer's empty-spot search, writes nothing persisted, and says in its own scope note that the path is an unreached fallback. VERDICT ON 60/61: ACCEPT — there was nothing to re-seat. Measured here at exactly this pair rather than inferred: all twelve circuit files of the two examples load, seat-on-disk equals seat-after-load on all six primary benches (dropped=[] for every one), and the nets are bb1:n-col-*. The three net-lgc-* nets in the pair are in the mega and stc12 VARIANTS only, joining arduino_mega to seven_seg_3 — two kinds with no breadboard footprint, so a logical net is the only correct answer, and the Mega has read `noseat` in every revision of that file. The flat twins drop their seats at load, which is fromJSON's pre-existing seat-without-a-breadboard rule and not this bump. What actually moved those benches' partitionShas was sb3-creator 33265cc, a part-id rename (mcu1 -> mega1 / stc151); the two variants whose id stayed mcu1 have unchanged shas, which is the control. The claim that they were unseated came from test/COVERAGE-ASSERT-PHYSICS.md, now RETRACTED: all 46 of its "no circuit file" rows are false and assert-physics passes both examples. BUMPED 2026-08-29 (fab-sbx) from 60fd117 to 14efc75, and the bump is FORCED by one item rather than routine: a kind alias outranked a registered engine model. KIND_ALIASES mapped `74hc595` onto the built-in `shift_register`, which declares twelve abstract terminals and NO vcc and NO gnd, so every 74hc595 in this corpus was rewritten to the power-less kind at fromJSON and nine seated variants of 08-led-chaser-595 had eighteen power connections landing on terminals the loaded part does not declare. resolveKind now asks the engine first for kinds in the new ENGINE_MODEL_WINS set — the alias is KEPT, so a file loaded against an engine that still lacks the model collapses exactly as before, and that backwards case is the mutation proof in cui's test/kind-alias-engine-model.test.js. MEASURED HERE, because the obvious story is wrong: no wire was ever dropped and nothing moves electrically. Across all 42 corpus files naming either kind, solved net counts and LED brightness are IDENTICAL either side (08-led-chaser-595's stc12 bench: 70 nets before, 70 after). What changes is the part's DECLARATION — sr1 now loads as `74hc595` with 35 terminals and sr1.vcc sits on bb1:rail-t+ at 5.0000 V as a terminal it actually has — and with it the model's own read('vcc'): board.js takes the built-in's VIH/VIL from the BOARD's global rail, the registered model from its own supply pin. cui's wire-resolution gate over this corpus is 259/259 green at 14efc75, and cui CI 33279345146 is green on it. The range 60fd117..14efc75 also carries fab-gate's browser-scenario work, which touches no model file.
